mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in initial jobless claims (UNRATE) predicts a contractionary demand shock that reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls >2% YoY and UNRATE rises >0.3pp MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200k for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts corporate profit margins and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero in at least 80% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >0.5% MoM for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.2% month-over-month signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls >0.2% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 65% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below 1,000 units for six consecutive months signals a protracted housing downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on broader GDP growth, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) to below 3.5% while nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) continue to rise signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressure and inflation risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the 10-year moving average for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which reduces consumer spending and dampens corporate revenue growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 10-year moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.
